newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: After Wednesday's volatility, it was a lacklustre day on the South African bond and forex markets with long bonds ending near their previous closing levels as investors took to the sidelines.
The rand had an equally dull day, holding in a narrow 4.4450 to 4.4600 range as players squared positions ahead of the 1997/1998 budget due next Wednesday.
Bond traders said the market was hampered by a lack of direction after a flood of fresh news on Wednesday and participants were reshuffling positions as budget fever set in.
"There was nothing driving the market today and the guys are cautious ahead of next week," a trader at a big local bank said.

The high money market shortage -- still over 11 billion rand on Wednesday -- was a worrying factor but this had been offset to some extent by better U.S. Treasuries after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said nothing to spook financial markets on Wednesday.
"I expect the market to trade on the lower side before the budget but nothing dramatic," a second trader said.
At 1405 GMT the key R150 bond was unchanged from its previous close of 15 percent after trading close to the figure throughout the day.
Players would be keeping an eye on U.S. Treasuries on Friday which were awaiting U.S. non farms payrolls data for signs of when, rather than if, U.S. interest rates would be raised, dealers said.

Foreigners sold a net 367.16 million rands worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 133.00 million on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said. Nominal cumulative volumes were 9.63 billion rand on Wednesday from 5.95 billion rand on Tuesday.
The rand ended an uneventful day slightly weaker on the U.S. dollar and traders said it was unlikely there would be any major moves over the next few days.
At 1405 GMT the unit was at 4.4570/4600 against the dollar from 4.4500/4530 overnight.
"There's no major news due aside from the budget and most people are squaring positions ahead of the event," one forex trader said.
He expected a 4.44 to 4.47 band on Friday and at the start of next week, adding that volumes had slowed down considerably.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.1756/1849 on sterling from 7.1594/1719 and at 0.3856/3860 marks from 0.3844/3850 marks previously.
South Africa's money market shortage was at 11.393 billion rand on Wednesday from 11.395 billion rand on Tuesday -- its highest level in over 14 months, the Reserve Bank said.
Three-month NCD rates were quoted unchanged between 16.55 and 16.70 percent and the 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
